newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Yachting-Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.
newsitem.headline: Australian Yachting-Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.

text.p: By Peter Campbell*
WINTER SAILING BOOMS

You won't find too many sailors at the footie this winter, judging by the massive entry the Cruising Yacht Club of Australia has received for its Sunday Winter Series on Sydney Harbour which begins this weekend.

The block entry as of Friday totalled 151 and the Club expects that Sunday fleets could reach as many as 180 yachts with casual entries coming in on sunny winter days. The Winter series runs through May, June and July with 14 pointscore races.

Sailing in eight divisions, entries range from the CYCA Youth Sailing Academy's Elliott 5.9 sports sloops through to the biggest ocean racing yachts like PETER WALKER'S Foxtel Amazon and WARWICK MILLER's Exile which fought out line honours in the recent Sydney-Mooloolaba ocean race.

MILLER, with his enthusiastic support for yachting since returning to live in Sydney, has donated a swagful of his Hong Kong-made Guess watches as trophies for the Winter Series to add to the Club's traditional prizes of jackets.

CYCA Commodore PETER BUSH will make a welcome return to racing with his recently acquired sloop Kidnapped, clearly more relaxed after the near simultaneous trauma of a shoulder operation amid the drama of the biscuit poisoning scare at Arnotts where he is marketing director.

Other prominent yachting business and professional people turning out for the Winter Series include mariner owner ROBIN CRAWFORD with Assassin, children's book publisher JOHN GILDER with the aptly named Beneteau 42, Story Teller, surgeon MICHAEL QUINN with Sycorax, travel agency boss BOB STEEL with his Mooloolaba race IMS division winner, Quest, chartered accountant and CYCA Rear Commodore ED PSALTIS helming Midnight Rambler, and Ord Minet CEO Chris Gorman sailing Adria which he skippered to a PHS overall win in the recent Sydney-Mooloolaba race.
OLD SALT BACK FOR GREAT VETERANS RACE

Despite a stroke and five heart by-passes over the past three years, Sydney waterfront and sailing identity BOY MESSENGER will take the helm again on Sunday in the Cruising Yacht Club of Australia's annual Great Veterans Race, a feature event on the opening day of the Winter Series.

The Great Veterans Race will bring together 15 former ocean racing yachts which contested Sydney-Hobart races between 1945 and 1965, among them three winners of line and handicap honours and one yacht which contested in the inaugural 1945 Hobart.

But it won't be just old yachts competing, many old salts will be back on deck again, including 72-year-old MESSENGER who will steer Malohi, the yacht which 35 years ago he helped SYD FISCHER sail in his first Sydney-Hobart.

Sunday's Great Veterans Race will also see the return of the famous cutter Winston Churchill which was second boat to finish to Rani in the inaugural Sydney-Hobart and went on to compete in 16 Hobarts, including the 50th in 1994.

Now owned by RICHARD WINNING, Winston Churchill will competing with past Hobart line honours winners BRUCE GOULD'S Margaret Rintoul (1950 and 1951) and NIGEL STOKES' Fidelis (1996), along with SIR JAMES HARDY's always well provisioned gaff-rigger Nerida which won Hobart on corrected time in 1950.
LACHLAN MURDOCH JOINS CYCA

We didn't notice his yacht among the 151 entries for the Winter Series, but a newly elected member of the Cruising Yacht Club is LACHLAN MURDOCH, this week named as the new boss of the Australian arm of News Corp, taking over from KEN COWLEY.

LACHLAN is the proud owner of Tall Cotton, the much admired Swan 65 berthed at the outer end of Marina C. While he has yet to follow in father RUPERT'S wake by competing in a Sydney-Hobart (Ilina 1964, Sayonara 1995) he is certainly showing enthusiasm for the sport.
Maybe a maxi yacht owner of the future?
EXCLUSIVE YACHT RACES
The annual Fujitsu Gosford-Lord Howe Island race and the Tag Heuer Ansett Big Boat Series at Hayman Island are now the most exclusive yachting event in Australia.
Notices of Race for both the Lord Howe Island and Hayman Island events were released this week, with the Lord Howe race restricted to 25 yachts and Hayman Island to 20 boats.

The limit on the fleet for Lord Howe, which starts on Saturday October 25 is because of the delicate environmental state of the lagoon at the World Heritage-listed island, 420 nautical miles north-east of Sydney.

The limit of 20 yachts, by invitation only, for the up-market Hayman Island Resort Big Boat Series, is because there is no more room at the inn (marina) and because they obviously don't want too many noisy yachties ashore among the guests.
The Big Boat Series will comprise six day races in the waters of the Whitsunday Islands, from August 17-21, the longest 45 nautical miles.
BOAT SHOW CELBRATES 30 YEARS

Motor racing legend DICK JOHNSON has taken on a new role -- promoting his other favourite pastime as patron of the 30th annual Sydney International Boat Show to be held at Darling Harbour from July 24-29.

The spectacular Boat Show will exhibit the latest in millions of dollars worth of craft from luxury motor cruisers and ocean-going yachts through to canoes, inflatables, highspeed runabouts, sailing dinghies, as well as a vast range of high tech marine equipment.

Strictly Sail will be another feature of this year's Show with sailing displays, seminars, on-water demonstrations and fashion parades, with the Yachting Association of New South Wales also organising a special sailing seminar.
WOMEN ARE WINNERS
The BETHWAITE family are on a roll, sailing-wise at least.

While CRA's managing director MARK BETHWAITE is out of the sailing scene at present, sorting out the company's rutile investments in Sierra Leone, his brother JULIAN'S boat-building activities are expanding internationally since the selection of the 49er for the Sydney 2000 Olympics, and his sister NICOLA is maintaining the status of women's sailing.
MARK, a former Flying Dutchman class representative at the Olympics and World champion in Solings and J24s, these days is content to sail a single-handed Laser on Sydney Harbour.
JULIAN seems too busy building the 49er, a high-performance skiff to go sailing, so it's been up to NICOLA keep the family name in the winner's list.

Back in February the former Olympic sailor won the Women on Water Nortel Asia Pacific Women's Regatta, sailing J24s, and last Sunday she won the Marinasses Women's Short Course Regatta, sailed in J24s.

NICOLA backed up on Sunday to steer One Step Ahead in the CYCA's Ladies Day Race, but had to be content with a sixth place. Winner was a member of another prominent Sydney sailing family, AMANDA WILMOT, steering Assassin.

Incidentally, AMANDA'S nephew, NATHAN, 17, and niece, SARAH, 15, have been chosen to skipper 420 class yachts at the International Sailing Federation's World Youth Sailing Championships in Japan in August. Their father is JAMIE WILMOT, a former World champion and Olympic sailor and successful offshore racing helmsman who himself sailed in Japan many years back, helming Seaflyer in the Quarter Ton Cup.
* Peter Campbell is editor of OFFSHORE Yachting magazine. -- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
